thread:
maria (ml-eng): Heads up — bringing up a quantized HF model in Redwood Dedicated and the embeddings don't match HF baseline. small but consistent drift. anyone seen this after conversion?

sam (nlp): how big is the drift? cosine? or just ranking differences?

maria (ml-eng): cosine avg ~0.12 drop vs hf pt, top-k rerank recall down ~3%. numbers from a 1k query eval.

toni (research): common culprits: special tokens mapping, tokenizer truncation side, or CLS vs mean pooling mismatch. did you convert the tokenizer with our conversion script or use raw HF files?

maria (ml-eng): used our converter: `convert_hf_to_redwood.py --model meta/llama-7b-quant --out /mnt/redwood/models/llama7q` but I forced the tokenizer copy.

sam (nlp): show `tokenizer.config` and `model.config`? especially fields: `add_bos_token`, `cls_token`, `pad_token`, `truncation_side`. Sometimes HF tokenizers have `bos_token` but convert script renames to `cls_token` or drops it.

maria (ml-eng): attached snippet: ```json
{"truncation_side": "left", "pad_token": "<pad>", "bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>"}
```

toni (research): aha — truncation_side left is suspicious. Our default in Redwood inference uses right truncation when generating embeddings (we keep prefix). If HF was truncating left, the token alignment changes and mean/cls pooling picks different tokens.

zack (infra): are we applying prefix KV-cache padding or doing pre-tokenization chunking? quant kernels sometimes require alignment to multiples of 8 which can add pad tokens. Could interact with pooling.

maria (ml-eng): we saw extra pad tokens at the start in the converted tokenizer. Some examples had `<pad>` at position 0 after decoding.

sam (nlp): two quick checks: 1) ensure `tokenizer.truncation_side` set to 'right' during conversion; 2) confirm whether Redwood's embedding pipeline uses `pooling=cls` or `pooling=mean`. Which one did your eval use?

maria (ml-eng): eval used cls pooling to match our reranker. Redwood default had mean pooling for that model. I switched to cls in the config and numbers got closer (cosine ~0.06 diff) but still not identical.

toni (research): remaining gap often from special token index mapping. HF might treat `<s>` as token 1 while our conversion put it at 0. Check `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<s>','</s>','<pad>'])`.

maria (ml-eng): ran that: HF ids [1,2,0], converted [0,2,1] — oof. So `<s>` and `<pad>` swapped. That explains weird embedding offsets for short inputs.

sam (nlp): fix: force token mapping during conversion: ```python
# conversion snippet
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('meta/llama-7b')
# enforce pad token index
tok.add_special_tokens({'pad_token':'<pad>'})
tok.backend_tokenizer.post_processor = ... # keep original ordering
tok.save_pretrained(out_dir)
```
But actual fixer: normalise special tokens order in `config.json` before saving.

zack (infra): also note quantized kernels sometimes reorder embeddings array in the model file layout. We had a bug in 2026-02 where embedding table stored transpose. That caused small but consistent cosine shifts. Check model artifact `embeddings.bin` header for byte-order magic.

maria (ml-eng): thanks — I will: 1) re-run conversion forcing truncation_side='right' and special token order; 2) set pooling to cls explicitly in Redwood model config; 3) re-run quantization with verify-embeddings flag.

eval-bot: quick eval summary: before fixes avg cosine=0.876 vs hf 0.995 baseline (delta 0.119). after forcing pooling=cls and truncation_right avg cosine=0.940 (delta 0.055). rerank recall@10 moved from 0.82 -> 0.86 (hf=0.89).

toni (research): solid improvement. After token id ordering fix and the infra check, we should be within noise. Also add unit test in conversion that compares 100 sample embeddings with HF and asserts cos > 0.98 to catch regressions.

sam (nlp): +1 for the unit test. Also log the tokenizer special token id map in the model manifest so runtime can sanity-check on load.

maria (ml-eng): will do. last q: should we default Redwood embed pipeline to prefer mean pooling for open models and cls only when flagged? Want to avoid silent behavior changes.

toni (research): prefer explicit config per model. defaulting to mean is fine but add a model-level `expected_pooling` field and a conversion step that sets it based on HF metadata or a mapping table.

zack (infra): I'll add a startup sanity-check that warns if `expected_pooling` != runtime pooling. emits a warning to logs and to the conversion report.

maria (ml-eng): perfect — I'll file a tiny PR to conversion script + add the unit test. thanks team :rocket:
